notes: Paper derives stellar cooling bounds on dark gauge bosons (Z') from U(1) extensions of the SM. Main results in Fig. 4 show bounds for B−L and Le−Lμ(τ) models. From text (Conclusions): 'For B−L and Le−Lμ(τ) models with m_Z' ≲10 keV, the gauge coupling g_Z' is constrained by the solar model to be at least below 4.1×10^-10 and 3.9×10^-11, respectively.' These are mass-independent (flat) bounds valid below ~10 keV, encoded as horizontal lines. The paper also discusses dark photon (kinetic mixing ε) and Lμ−Lτ models, but those have photon-like couplings with mass-dependent bounds that vanish at m→0. Confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the paper presents multiple coupling types and the primary focus is on theoretical production mechanisms rather than a single experimental exclusion limit; (2) the bounds are derived from astrophysical constraints (solar cooling) rather than direct measurements; (3) extracting the exact numerical limits requires careful reading of the conclusions and figure captions.
